source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Pomelo (ក្រូចថ្លុង) is a well-known Cambodian citrus fruit eaten fresh, valued both for home consumption and as a cash crop. The source gives a detailed nutrient composition table for pomelo juice/pulp per 100 grams, including water (~88.58g), ash, fiber, sugar, calcium, phosphorus, iron, and several vitamins - notably vitamin C at roughly 27 mg per 100 grams, along with smaller amounts of vitamins A, B1, B2, B3, B5, and B6.

Because it can be stored and transported for a relatively long time compared to some other fruit, pomelo is also processed and traded beyond the immediate local market. The source notes that Pursat orange (ក្រូចពោធិសាត់) similarly provides good vitamin C (about 60 mg per 100 ml of juice), and that lime (ក្រូចឆ្មារ) is commonly used as a cooking condiment - general citrus background shared across MAFF's citrus guides.
